utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called to order. Good afternoon to everybody. Madam Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-14-A, the Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. May I call for the appearances. For the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is myself, Norman Farrell, Ms. Sonja Boelaert-Suominen, and Ms. Nicola Bonfield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand there is a phone link with the friends. Is the phone link established?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I believe it is, Your Honour. This is Russell Hayman appearing for General Blaskic by phone, together with Anto Nobilo and Andrew Paley, also by phone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Hayman. May I first ask Mr. Blaskic if he understands the proceedings, if there is any problem. Can you understand the proceedings, Mr. Blaskic? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I understand the proceedings, and I can follow the proceedings. I don't have any problem with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, first I would like to ask Mr. -- to ask the Defence if there is any problem concerning the detention of Mr. Blaskic. In --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: In particular, if the health condition of Mr. Blaskic is good now after ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Mr. Hayman. Thank you for inquiring. General Blaskic's health is greatly improved. And at this time I believe he is off medication, but I would invite the Court to inquire of him directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Hayman. May I ask Mr. Blaskic if he can confirm what his counsel is now saying about his health. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm whatever my counsel has said. My health condition is now much improved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm happy to learn that. So let's proceed. I understand there are no questions concerning the detention, the detention conditions of Mr. Blaskic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: There are none, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So let's proceed with the -- with the case. As the parties know, we are -- we are now in the process of considering the fourth Rule 115 motion submitted by the appellant. We have already -- the Appeals Chamber has already the Prosecution response that was filed on the 18th of June, and a reply is expected by the 30th of June, as was indicated in my scheduling order. I understand there is -- well, I know there is a request for an extension of page limits presented by Mr. Hayman. May I ask the Prosecution what is their feeling about that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I've reviewed the request by the Defence and the two reasons they've set forward; one, that it's a large motion, and the other that the Prosecution has put in its annexes some material which they allege is argumentative. With respect, and with great respect to my colleagues, the Prosecution position is that doesn't warrant an extension of the page limits. The material contained in the annexes are not argumentative, they're actually references from the logbook and they simply just cite the logbook. So in an attempt to be of assistance to the Court, we listed all of it instead of just putting a footnote where the Court would hen have to go and find all the references themselves. So as far as the Prosecution is concerned, there's nothing in the two paragraphs which warrant an extension of time -- an extension of the page limits on that basis and we'll be filing something to that effect by tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. So if I understand well, the Prosecution intends to submit a written response to that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes. We can submit one first thing tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll wait for the -- for the response, and then I will take a decision on this matter. There is another matter I wanted to -- to raise here, and it concerns the possibility of filing of rebuttal evidence. I indicated in my scheduling order that I would like to Prosecution to say something on this point; first if the Prosecution intends to file rebuttal evidence, and second, if -- what time would be required for such a submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, in compliance with your order, Your Honour, we have reviewed the material. First of all, it's my understanding that the rebuttal material you're requesting is at this stage of the proceedings prior to a determination of what would be admitted. So a somewhat different procedure than the first one. If my understanding is correct, then the Prosecution has rebuttal evidence in two forms; one is simply a cross-reference to the previous rebuttal material filed. We won't refile it, we'll just indicate which documents are relevant for your consideration. And secondly, any new documents, I expect that we have probably only around 15 -- there's around 15 or 20 new documents we're looking at now for rebuttal purposes. And I think the cross-references of the old, the drafting of the brief, and the filing of the however many it turns out to be - 15, let's say - probably we can do within four weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Indeed, it's my -- my intention to proceed with -- to have the rebuttal evidence before we make a decision on the fourth -- on the fourth motion. So four weeks would be your need.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: You cannot accelerate it a bit? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I can certainly try to do it within three weeks. The difficulty with cross-referencing is all the old documents, but I think three to four weeks would be -- certainly we can try to do it within three weeks, if that would be of more assistance to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Because indeed it would be good for the Court to have the rebuttal evidence and possibly the response before the recess, if we can make it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Of course. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: In order to be -- to process all this and make a decision maybe in -- in September on the -- on the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, do you have any comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as the Court will see when it reviews our fourth Rule 115 motion, although the documents are new to us, much of the subject matter is the same type of material we had been finding previously in the Croatian archives and so forth. So my concern would be if the Prosecutor has 20 documents that it newly discovered since its last submission of rebuttal evidence, then so be it. But if these were documents they previously had and that they were germane to our earlier motions, the question would be why do we have to delay the proceedings now another month for them to submit this material which they already had earlier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Hayman. May I turn to the Prosecution. Do they have anything to comment upon this?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Considering the arguments are new ones in the fourth additional evidence motion, I can't perceive that the Prosecution would have responded to those arguments, for example, the ABiH documents which were put in for the first time in the fourth motion. It would be a little bit difficult for us to foresee that as a possibility and respond to it when they've never put it in before. In fact, I note that these documents have been in the Defence possession since October 2001. If there's any delay here, if the Defence would have filed these with their last motion, we would have addressed it then. But it's not a matter of overlap; there are new issues raised in the fourth motion. We'll respond to them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Hayman, without prolonging the debate on this, but if you have any comment, you may make it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If they are no issues, Your Honour, so be it. If they are old issues, then I would still pose the question if they had the documents previously, should we delay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I think that I will press on the Prosecution to try to come within three weeks. And then we will see where we stand. And of course the Defence will have time to -- to respond to the rebuttal -- to the rebuttal evidence. Is this agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Prosecution, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: It's fine. Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Well, there is one -- one small other matter I wanted to raise. Mr. Hayman, in a couple of occasions you have indicated that it would -- the Defence would file a public version on the -- of the fourth Rule 115 motion. Can you perhaps indicate how long it would take to have that public version?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask Mr. Paley to address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PALEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe we should have that filed sometime next week. The delay was we had inquired from the Prosecution whether there were any documents that they considered to be confidential that needed to be redacted from the public version. I understand Mr. Farrell was in Africa for some period of time. We do now have the Prosecution's response to our inquiry. And as soon as we have our reply brief to the 115 motion filed, we will immediately take care of getting the public version of the motion filed with the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Paley. So I get that next week or immediately afterwards that the public version will be -- will be filed. It's important it's done as soon as possible, as it may affect the other motions for access to evidence. I mean, so -- to this motion, to this fourth motion. So it's important to have the public version as soon as possible. Well, are there any other matters that the parties want to raise? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: None for the Defence, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, if that is not the case, we can certainly adjourn now. The Status Conference stands adjourned.
